thesis: Emmy Noether proved that every continuous symmetry in physics comes with a conserved quantity, linking energy to time and momentum to space, and helped modernise abstract algebra. Her mathematics of symmetry now shapes neural networks designed to respect rotations and shifts.

story.title: Symmetry means conservation
story.text: Noether proved that every continuous symmetry of a physical system comes with a conserved quantity. Laws that are the same in every direction conserve angular momentum. Laws that are the same at every moment conserve energy. Physicists still use her theorem to find new conservation laws.

story.title: Round bowl, steady spin
story.text: A puck rolling in a perfectly round bowl feels the same forces however the bowl is turned. That rotational symmetry keeps its angular momentum fixed, so it sweeps out equal areas in equal times. In an oval bowl the symmetry breaks: angular momentum swings, but energy is still conserved because the laws do not change over time.

story.title: Symmetry built into AI
story.text: The link to AI is indirect, a shared idea rather than her theorem. Equivariant neural networks build symmetry into their design using group theory, the mathematics Noether helped modernise. When a molecule is turned, the predicted forces turn with it, so the network never has to learn every angle separately.
